rows: Honeybees perform a waggle dance to tell nestmates where food is located. Most stingless bee species, ______ lay scent trails that lead other foragers directly to the source.
The two sentences describe different ways of sharing a food location, so the second needs a contrast word. The scent trail is not an example, a result, or a restatement of the dance.
In the 1930s, engineers in the Netherlands completed a 32-kilometer dam that closed off a shallow inlet from the North Sea. ______ the saltwater inlet gradually became a freshwater lake.
Closing off the sea caused the inlet to turn fresh, so the second sentence is a result of the first.
Many desert plants have features that limit water loss. The saguaro cactus, ______ has a waxy skin and opens its pores only at night.
The saguaro is one specific case of the general claim about desert plants, so an example word fits.
Urban trees lower summer temperatures by shading pavement. ______ their leaves release water vapor, which cools the surrounding air.
The second sentence adds another way trees cool a city. It does not replace, oppose, or result from the first point.
Woodblock printing can demand weeks of carving for a single image. ______ many contemporary artists still choose the technique, valuing a texture that digital tools cannot match.
The first sentence gives a drawback, and the second says artists choose the technique anyway. That calls for a word meaning 'in spite of this'.

To date a wooden beam, a researcher first drills out a thin core and measures the width of each tree ring. ______ she compares the pattern of wide and narrow rings with a regional record whose dates are already known.
The word 'first' signals steps in a process, and the second sentence gives the step that follows.
Octopuses can change skin color within a second to blend into a reef. ______ cuttlefish adjust both the color and the texture of their skin to match nearby sand or rock.
Both animals do the same kind of thing, so a comparison word fits. Cuttlefish camouflage is not caused by octopus camouflage, and it is not a summary.
The poet revised her manuscript for eleven years and published fewer than forty poems in her lifetime. ______ she valued precision far more than volume.
The second sentence says what the facts in the first sentence mean, so it restates the same idea in different terms.
Early forecasters assumed the comet would brighten steadily as it neared the Sun. ______ it broke apart weeks before its closest approach and faded from view.
What happened took the place of what was expected, so a word meaning 'in place of that' is needed.
Sloths are often described as lazy, but their slowness is an effective survival strategy. ______ by moving so little, they avoid the notice of predators that hunt by detecting motion.
The second sentence supports and strengthens the claim that slowness helps sloths survive. It does not oppose the claim or come later in time.

A city survey found that residents living near new bike lanes drove less often than before. ______ bus service in the same neighborhoods doubled during that period, so the drop in driving cannot be credited to the lanes alone.
The second sentence complicates the finding by giving another possible cause. 'As a result' is tempting, but the bus service was not caused by the drop in driving.

Glass frogs sleep on green leaves, where red blood would normally make them visible to predators. While resting, the frogs store most of their red blood cells in the liver. ______ their bodies become far more transparent.
Hiding the red blood cells causes the transparency, so the last sentence is a result of the one before it.
The museum's new wing doubles the space available for exhibitions. It ______ includes a workshop where visitors can watch conservators repair paintings.
The workshop is a second feature of the wing, so an addition word fits.
Regular exercise strengthens the heart and lungs. ______ it has been linked to better sleep and improved mood.
Better sleep and mood are further benefits, not examples or results of a stronger heart.
The library lends books, films, and music free of charge. ______ it offers weekly classes on using computers.
The classes are one more service, so the sentence adds to the list.
The proposed bridge would cut travel time between the two towns in half. ______ it would give emergency vehicles a route that stays open during floods.
The second sentence adds a further, weightier benefit of the bridge.
Maya decided not to enter the race this year because her ankle had not fully healed. ______ the entry fee had doubled since last spring.
The fee is an extra reason for the same decision. It is not a result of the injury.
The new battery stores twice as much energy as the model it replaces. ______ it can be manufactured without the rare metals that made the old one so costly.
The second advantage builds on the first, so a word that adds a stronger point fits.
Coral reefs shelter thousands of species in a small area of ocean. ______ tropical rainforests hold an enormous variety of life on a small share of the land.
Reefs and rainforests are alike in the way described, so a comparison word is needed.
A vaccine trains the immune system by exposing it to a harmless piece of a virus. ______ a flight simulator prepares pilots by exposing them to emergencies that carry no real danger.
Both sentences describe safe practice for a real threat, so the pattern is the same.
Mount Everest rises about 8,800 meters above sea level. ______ the tallest peak in the Alps, Mont Blanc, reaches roughly 4,800 meters.
The two heights are set side by side, so a word that introduces a comparison fits.
A teacher who praises every answer gives students no way to tell strong work from weak. ______ a critic who condemns every film gives readers no guidance about which ones to avoid.
The same reasoning applies to both cases: judging everything alike tells people nothing. The critic is not an example of a teacher.
Sound travels through air at about 340 meters per second. ______ light covers nearly 300,000 kilometers in the same time.
The two speeds are very different, so a contrast word fits.
Renting an apartment offers the freedom to move on short notice. Buying a home, ______ allows a family to build savings through ownership.
Buying is the opposing option with a different advantage.
Sales of printed newspapers have fallen for two decades. ______ the number of people reading news on phones has climbed every year.
Two opposite trends happened over the same period. The passage does not say one caused the other.
Many people picture deserts as endless seas of sand dunes. ______ most desert land is covered by bare rock and gravel.
The second sentence corrects a common picture with the true situation.
Travelers can reach the island by taking the morning ferry from the harbor. ______ they can book a seat on the small plane that leaves each afternoon.
The plane is a second option in place of the ferry.
When interest rates fall, people tend to borrow and spend more. ______ when rates rise, borrowing becomes costly and spending slows.
The second sentence gives the reverse situation and the reverse outcome.
The long winter did not weaken the colony of bees. ______ the hive emerged in spring with more workers than it had in autumn.
The first sentence denies an idea, and the second states that the opposite happened.
The author did not write the novel to entertain. ______ she meant it as a warning about the cost of ignoring history.
After a 'did not' statement, the second sentence gives the correct purpose in its place.
The climbers lost two days to storms and ran low on fuel. ______ they reached the summit before the end of the week.
They succeeded in spite of the setbacks.
Electric cars cost more to buy than comparable gasoline models. ______ many drivers find that lower fuel and repair bills make up the difference within a few years.
The second sentence accepts the higher price but argues it is outweighed.
The orchestra had only three rehearsals before opening night. ______ critics praised the performance as the best of the season.
Little rehearsal would predict a weak performance, yet the reviews were excellent.
The new medicine relieved symptoms in most patients who took it. ______ doctors want larger studies before recommending it widely.
The good result is granted, but caution remains. 'Therefore' would wrongly make the caution a result of the success.
Forecasters could not agree on whether the storm would reach the coast. ______ the city opened its shelters and told residents to prepare.
The city acted whatever the forecast turned out to be.
Solar panels can supply most of a household's electricity on a bright day. ______ they produce nothing at night, so homes need batteries or a connection to the grid.
The second sentence admits an obvious limit on the claim just made.
The committee's report is thorough and carefully researched. ______ it overlooks how much the proposed changes would cost small schools.
The praise stands, but the second sentence limits it with a criticism.
The mayor wants to attract new businesses with lower taxes. ______ she recognizes that the city cannot afford to cut funding for its schools.
Two aims that pull against each other are both true for the mayor.
The team's new strategy has produced five straight wins. ______ four of those games were against the weakest opponents in the league.
The second sentence concedes a weakness in the evidence for the strategy.
Handwritten letters are a better way to stay close to distant friends than quick text messages. ______ letters take days to arrive, but the care they show is worth the wait.
The writer admits a point for the other side before returning to the main claim.
The old factory district has become one of the city's liveliest neighborhoods. ______ a few buildings still stand empty, but most now hold shops, studios, and cafes.
The sentence admits an exception and then reaffirms the main point after 'but'.
Lena knew the bakery would probably be sold out by noon. ______ she walked across town in the hope that one loaf was left.
She went in spite of what she knew. 'Accordingly' would mean she acted in line with it.
The treaty was criticized by leaders in both countries. ______ it was approved by large majorities in each parliament.
Approval came in spite of the criticism.
The bridge inspection found cracks in two of the main supports. ______ the city closed the bridge to traffic until repairs could be made.
The closure is the logical result of the cracks.
Honey contains very little water and is highly acidic, so bacteria cannot grow in it. ______ sealed jars of honey can remain safe to eat for decades.
The long shelf life follows from the fact that bacteria cannot grow.
Each tree in the orchard was grown from a cutting of the same parent. ______ all of the trees are genetically identical.
Identical genes are the consequence of a shared parent.
The village sits in a valley that floods every spring. ______ its oldest houses were built on tall stone foundations.
The flooding explains why the houses were built high.
The survey showed that most riders wanted buses to run later at night. ______ the transit agency extended service on its busiest routes until midnight.
The agency acted in a way that fits what the survey showed.
Warmer ocean water causes more moisture to evaporate into the air. This added moisture, ______ feeds heavier rainfall when storms form.
One effect becomes the cause of the next in a chain.
No one was surprised when Dr. Osei was chosen to lead the expedition. ______ she had spent twenty years studying the region's glaciers.
The second sentence gives the reason for the first. 'As a result' reverses the direction: her experience caused the choice, not the other way round.
The school wants every student to read at grade level by the end of third grade. ______ it has hired four reading specialists and lengthened the daily reading period.
The hiring and the longer period are steps taken to reach the stated goal.
Young children learn best in short bursts of focused activity. ______ the museum designed its new exhibit as a series of five-minute stations.
The design was guided by the fact stated in the first sentence.
The wetland is the only nesting site for several rare birds. ______ it is protected by law from any new construction.
Because the wetland is that kind of place, the protection follows.
Some animals use tools to get food. Sea otters, ______ crack open shellfish by striking them against rocks.
Sea otters are one case of the general statement.
The study examined how sleep affects memory. ______ researchers tested whether students who slept eight hours recalled more vocabulary than those who slept five.
The second sentence narrows the broad topic to the exact thing tested.
The storm damaged crops across the region. ______ apple growers lost nearly their entire harvest.
Apple growers are singled out as a notable case of the wider damage.
A small change in habit can produce a large effect over time. ______ a person who saves five dollars a day will have set aside more than eighteen hundred dollars in a year.
The savings figure is a concrete case that shows the general claim.
The council has good reasons to reject the plan for a new parking garage. ______ the site floods whenever the river rises.
The flooding is the first of the promised reasons.
The recipe depends on two ingredients that are hard to find in winter, ______ fresh basil and ripe tomatoes.
The sentence goes on to name exactly which two ingredients were meant.
The Great Wall of China is often said to be visible from the Moon. ______ it cannot be seen from that distance without a telescope.
The second sentence gives the real situation in place of a popular belief.
The first edition of the atlas was a success. ______ it sold out within a week and had to be reprinted twice that year.
The second sentence confirms the claim and makes it stronger. It does not oppose it.
The new schedule saves the company money on electricity. ______ it gives employees two extra hours each week with their families.
A second benefit is added and ranked above the first.
Several cities have cut traffic deaths by redesigning their streets. ______ Oslo recorded no pedestrian deaths in 2019.
Oslo is pointed out as a striking case worth noticing.
It is hard to say which invention changed daily life the most. ______ the printing press belongs near the top of any list.
After admitting doubt, the writer stresses one thing that is beyond doubt.
A good field guide should be light, sturdy, and clearly illustrated. ______ it must be accurate, because a single wrong identification can be dangerous.
Accuracy is presented as the most important quality of all.
The species is nocturnal; ______ it sleeps during the day and hunts at night.
The second half explains what the word 'nocturnal' means.
For every dollar the program spends, the city saves three dollars in later health costs. ______ the program more than pays for itself.
The second sentence states the same fact in simpler terms.
The contract runs to forty pages of rules about deadlines, payments, and penalties. ______ it says that the builder will be paid only when each stage is finished on time.
The second sentence boils the long contract down to its core idea.
The new rule requires a permit that costs more than most street vendors earn in a month. ______ it bans small vendors from the market.
The rule is not called a ban, but in practice it works as one.
Making paper by hand takes several steps. ______ plant fibers are soaked and beaten into a watery pulp.
Soaking the fibers has to come at the start of the process.
______ the company sold its bread only at a single weekend market. Within five years, its loaves were stocked by grocery stores in three states.
The first sentence describes how things stood at the beginning, before the growth.
In 2006, astronomers reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet. ______ it had been counted as the ninth planet of the solar system.
'Had been counted' places the second sentence before the 2006 change.
The scientist won a national prize in 2020 for her work on batteries. ______ she had spent a decade studying how metals corrode.
'Had spent' shows that the decade of study came before the prize.
The potter shapes the clay on a wheel and leaves it to dry for several days. ______ she fires it in a kiln to harden it.
Firing is the step that follows drying.
As a teenager, Rosa repaired radios in her uncle's shop. ______ she used that experience to design communication equipment for ships.
The design work came at a later point in her life.
The players shook hands and collected their medals. ______ they gathered on the field for a team photograph.
The photograph followed the medal ceremony in time.
The seedling grew only a few centimeters a year in the shade of older trees. ______ a storm opened a gap in the canopy, and the young tree shot upward.
The change came after a long period of slow growth.
The cook washes the rice, toasts it in oil, and simmers it in broth. ______ she stirs in fresh herbs just before serving.
Adding the herbs is the last step in the series.
The city's first subway line opened in 1975 with six stations. ______ the system has four lines and carries half a million riders a day.
The present tense 'has' and 'carries' shows the second sentence is about now.
The two inventors argued for years over who deserved credit for the design. ______ a court ruled that they should share the patent.
The ruling is the final outcome of a long dispute.
The new bridge will not open until next summer. ______ drivers must use the ferry or take the long route around the bay.
The second sentence covers the period between now and the opening.
The manuscript was rejected by eleven publishers. ______ it was accepted by a small press and became a bestseller.
The acceptance came after the rejections.
The drummer keeps a steady beat with her feet. ______ her hands play a faster, shifting rhythm on the cymbals.
Both actions happen at the same moment.
Farmers once relied on almanacs and experience to decide when to plant. ______ they turn to satellite data and soil sensors.
The second sentence describes a practice that is growing over time, in contrast with 'once'.
The lighthouse was badly damaged by a storm in 1921. ______ ships entering the harbor were guided by a lamp mounted on a nearby hill.
The lamp was used from the time of the storm onward.
This essay has shown that the canal lowered shipping costs, drew new industries to the region, and tripled the town's population. ______ the canal transformed the local economy.
The last sentence closes the essay with its overall judgment.
The report finds that the park is used by more people, costs less to maintain, and has less litter than it did five years ago. ______ the renovation has succeeded on every measure the city tracks.
The second sentence gathers the listed findings into one statement.
A few stores on Main Street saw sales dip during the festival, and one closed early because of the crowds. ______ local businesses earned far more that weekend than in a typical week.
The second sentence gives the picture for all businesses taken together, after a few exceptions.
The apartment was small, dark, noisy, and far from the nearest train station. ______ it had almost nothing to recommend it.
The list of faults is boiled down to one brief judgment.
Some of the volunteers arrived late, and a few left before the work was finished. ______ the cleanup went smoothly and the beach was clear by noon.
Considering everything, the day went well in spite of small problems.
The drug lowered blood pressure, caused few side effects, and cost less than existing treatments. ______ the trial gave doctors every reason to be hopeful.
The three results add up to the judgment in the second sentence.
It rained on the first morning and the tent leaked, but the hikes were beautiful and the food was good. ______ the family counted the trip a success.
Weighing the good against the bad leads to an overall verdict.
Seedlings must be watered every day during their first two weeks. ______ their shallow roots dry out and the plants die.
The second sentence says what happens if the watering is not done.
The forecast says heavy snow may close the mountain pass tomorrow. ______ the team will travel tonight and stay near the stadium.
The plan applies if the pass does close.
Researchers suspect that the ancient jars once held olive oil. ______ traces of plant fats should still be detectable in the clay.
The prediction holds only if the suspicion is correct.
Historians disagree about whether the bridge was finished in 1310 or 1320. ______ it has carried travelers across the river for some seven centuries.
Whichever date is right, the second statement is true.
The company may repair the old machines or replace them with new ones. ______ the factory will be closed for at least two weeks.
The closure happens under both options.
Individual results varied from one school to another. ______ students who ate breakfast scored higher on morning tests than those who did not.
After noting variation, the sentence states what was true in most cases.
The river froze in late October this year. ______ ice does not form on it until the middle of December.
The second sentence gives the usual pattern, which this year broke.
A handful of the letters in the collection deal with politics. ______ they describe the ordinary routines of farm life.
After a small exception, the sentence says what most of the letters contain.
The editor made an exception and published the anonymous essay. ______ the magazine prints only work that is signed by its author.
The word 'exception' sets up a statement of the normal practice.
The fire spread through the warehouse within minutes. ______ the building was empty, and no one was hurt.
The second sentence is good news after a dangerous event.
The restored theater was ready to reopen in time for its hundredth anniversary. ______ a burst pipe flooded the stage two days before the celebration.
The second sentence is bad news that spoils the plan.
The tiny shrew weighs less than a coin. ______ it can eat about its own body weight in food each day.
Such a large appetite is unexpected in so small an animal.
The marine biologist spent her career studying sea turtles. ______ the research ship launched in her honor carries a turtle on its flag.
The turtle on the flag suits the work she was known for.
The lecture will cover the history of the city's water system. ______ the hall where it will be held was once a pumping station.
The second sentence adds a loosely related side fact.
The old mill stands at the edge of the river, its wheel still turning. ______ a row of stone cottages once housed the families who worked there.
The second sentence moves to another spot close to the mill. Nothing is caused, restated, or conceded.
In the northern valleys, farmers lost most of their wheat to the late frost. ______ the harvest was close to normal.
The second sentence shifts to other places, where the outcome was different.
From the lookout, hikers can see the lake directly below them. ______ a line of snow-covered peaks marks the border between the two countries.
The view moves from what is close to what is far away.
The east bank of the canal is lined with warehouses and loading docks. ______ gardens slope down to the water from a row of old houses.
The description crosses from one bank of the canal to the other.
The trail first crosses a meadow full of wildflowers. ______ it climbs through pine forest to a rocky ridge.
The second sentence describes a later stretch of the same trail.
Last spring the river rose over its banks and flooded the lower streets. This year, heavy rains have ______ pushed the water past the flood line.
The flooding is happening a second time.
The first trial showed that the coating kept steel from rusting. ______ in the second trial, the coated samples showed no damage after a year in salt water.
The second trial repeated the result of the first.
The opening chapter explained that the survey reached only city residents. ______ this limit means the results say little about rural areas.
The sentence points back to a limit the text has already described.
At the start of the meeting, the director said the budget had been cut by a tenth. ______ that cut means the summer program cannot grow this year, she reminded the staff before closing.
The director is returning to a point she made at the start of the meeting.
